line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nxd4 Qxd4
teaches: Trading a knight in the centre because it is 'just a trade' is how a position quietly goes wrong — count what stands there afterwards: if the recapture puts their queen in the middle where nothing can chase her, you have spent a developed piece to improve the strongest piece they own. A trade is only equal when the square it leaves behind is.
explains: The queen recaptures on d4 in the centre, holding the pawn on e4 and the knight on c3 while eyeing the knight on f6 and the pawn on a7. The trade removed a defender and gave the queen the best square on the board.
